sources.location: https://ftp.pride.ebi.ac.uk/pride/data/archive/2018/02/PXD005931/ (Janus_MascotSearch.dat, RB_161031_Aplha1acid_HCD_15.dat headers; RAW headers read by HTTP range)

claims.evidence: PRIDE organism and organismParts; paper Methods: 'men diagnosed with ... prostate cancer'
PRIDE disease field; paper: all 24 donors are prostate cancer patients (12 localized, 12 high-risk/metastatic)
No mapping of runs to case/control groups available; each file is a distinct donor (Janus_<n> from the file name)
Paper Methods and RAW headers ('Method of Q Exactive'); embedded acquisition paths match file names for all 24
Paper and PRIDE protocol (stepped NCE 15, 25, 35); RAW method name HCD_120min_Top7_Quickstart_NCE15_35

claims.value: Carbamidomethyl C fixed; Oxidation M variable; Glyco_Fuc_HexNAc variable

limitations: PRIDE text says serum from 'healthy individuals and prostate cancer patients' while the paper Methods describe all 24 donors as prostate cancer patients; the paper was followed (disease = prostate adenocarcinoma, per PRIDE disease field).

Mapping of Janus numbers to the two clinical groups (localized vs high-risk/metastatic) is not deposited in files read (the 5 GB .rov Distiller file was not parsed); no factor value was added, and age/ancestry/individual are not available.

Biological replicate set to 1 for all donors because no replicate structure is supported; RB_161102_JANUS39_TIO2.raw was acquired two days before the rest (161102 vs 161104) but is a serum sample with the same method.
The deposit contains no archives (.zip/.tar); only individual RAW files were claimed (29 RAW: 24 serum, 5 standards, each exactly once).
Glyco_Fuc_HexNAc (Mascot custom modification on the residue code O = HexNAc, 'fucose addition on HexNAc') has no Unimod entry; written without AC.
Reduction/alkylation reagents and enrichment process (TiO2) are described in the paper but not encoded (optional columns, ontology terms not verified).
